title: Polity Complete 3: Judiciary, States, UTs & Federalism

questions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the Supreme Court of India:
1. The strength of the Supreme Court is fixed at 34 judges, including the Chief Justice of India, by an Act of Parliament of 2019.
2. A judge of the Supreme Court retires at the age of 62 years.
3. A judge of the Supreme Court can be removed by the President after an address by each House, supported by a majority of the total membership and two-thirds of the members present and voting, in the same session.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: The Supreme Court (Number of Judges) Amendment Act, 2019 raised the strength from 31 to 34 including the CJI. Judges retire at 65 (High Court judges at 62), and removal on proved misbehaviour or incapacity needs the special majority in both Houses in the same session under Article 124(4).
questions.u: Supreme Court, High Court & Subordinate Courts

questions.q:
Match the following cases with their holdings:
A. First Judges Case (S. P. Gupta, 1981)
B. Second Judges Case (1993)
C. Third Judges Case (1998, Presidential Reference)
D. Fourth Judges Case (2015)
1. The collegium for Supreme Court appointments consists of the CJI and four senior-most judges
2. 'Consultation' with the CJI does not mean 'concurrence', giving the executive the upper hand
3. The opinion of the CJI has primacy, formed in consultation with the two senior-most judges
4. The National Judicial Appointments Commission was struck down
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
questions.e: S. P. Gupta gave the executive primacy, the Second Judges Case reversed it and created the collegium, the Third (Article 143 reference) expanded it to the CJI and four seniors, and the Fourth Judges Case struck down the NJAC.
questions.u: Supreme Court, High Court & Subordinate Courts

questions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the jurisdiction of the Supreme Court:
1. The original jurisdiction under Article 131 extends to disputes between a State and a private citizen.
2. Under Article 131, the Court has original jurisdiction in a dispute between the Government of India and one or more States on which the existence of a legal right depends.
3. The concept of a curative petition evolved in the Rupa Ashok Hurra case (2002).
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Article 131 covers only Centre-State and inter-State disputes, so a citizen's dispute with a State goes through other jurisdiction such as Article 32 or the ordinary courts. A curative petition is the last remedy after a review petition is dismissed, evolved to prevent miscarriage of justice.
questions.u: Supreme Court, High Court & Subordinate Courts

questions.q:
Statement-I: The advisory opinion of the Supreme Court under Article 143 is not binding on the President.
Statement-II: The Supreme Court is bound to answer every reference made to it by the President under Article 143(1).
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
o: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
questions.e: Article 143(1) says the Court 'may' give its opinion, and in 1993 the Court declined to answer the reference on the Ayodhya dispute. The opinion is only advisory and has persuasive value.
questions.u: Supreme Court, High Court & Subordinate Courts

questions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding writ jurisdiction:
1. The right to move the Supreme Court for enforcement of Fundamental Rights under Article 32 is itself a Fundamental Right.
2. A High Court can issue writs under Article 226 only for the enforcement of Fundamental Rights.
3. A High Court can issue a writ to any person or authority outside its territorial limits if the cause of action arises wholly or partly within its territory.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Article 226 allows writs for Fundamental Rights and for 'any other purpose', so a High Court's writ jurisdiction is wider than that of the Supreme Court under Article 32. The 15th Amendment added the cause of action rule in Article 226(2).
questions.u: Supreme Court, High Court & Subordinate Courts

questions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the High Courts:
1. A judge of a High Court retires at the age of 62 years.
2. A person is eligible to be a High Court judge if he has held a judicial office in India for at least ten years.
3. A High Court judge is removed by the President on the recommendation of the Chief Justice of India.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Article 217 gives ten years as a judicial officer or ten years as a High Court advocate, and the retirement age is 62. A High Court judge is removed in the same manner and on the same grounds as a Supreme Court judge, through Parliament, not on the CJI's recommendation.
questions.u: Supreme Court, High Court & Subordinate Courts

questions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the subordinate judiciary:
1. District judges are appointed by the Governor in consultation with the High Court.
2. The State Public Service Commission recommends the appointment of district judges.
3. The control over district courts and courts subordinate to them is vested in the High Court.
4. A person who is not in the service of the Union or the State can be appointed a district judge if he has been an advocate for at least seven years.
How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Articles 233 and 235 vest the key role in the High Court, which is the reason the lower judiciary is insulated from the executive. The State Public Service Commission is consulted for other judicial posts (Article 234), not for district judges.
questions.u: Supreme Court, High Court & Subordinate Courts

questions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding tribunals under the Constitution:
1. Part XIV-A on Tribunals was added by the 42nd Amendment Act.
2. Article 323A empowers both Parliament and State Legislatures to establish administrative tribunals.
3. Article 323B empowers the appropriate legislature to set up tribunals for matters such as taxation, industrial disputes and land reforms.
4. Following L. Chandra Kumar (1997), decisions of tribunals can be appealed directly to the Supreme Court bypassing the High Court.
How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Article 323A, for public service tribunals, lets only Parliament make the law, while 323B allows both Parliament and State Legislatures for the listed subjects. Chandra Kumar held that tribunals' decisions are subject to the High Courts' writ jurisdiction under Articles 226 and 227, before a Division Bench.
questions.u: Supreme Court, High Court & Subordinate Courts

questions.q: Under the Contempt of Courts Act, 1971, the maximum punishment for contempt of court is
o: simple imprisonment up to one year, or a fine up to Rs 5,000, or both
simple imprisonment up to three months, or a fine up to Rs 1,000, or both
simple imprisonment up to two years, or a fine up to Rs 10,000, or both
simple imprisonment up to six months, or a fine up to Rs 2,000, or both
questions.e: The Supreme Court and High Courts are courts of record under Articles 129 and 215 and can punish for their contempt. The 2006 amendment added truth as a defence if it is in public interest and bona fide.
questions.u: Supreme Court, High Court & Subordinate Courts

questions.q:
Consider the following pairs:
Case : Matter
1. Vishaka case : Guidelines against sexual harassment at the workplace
2. Olga Tellis case : Right to livelihood as part of the right to life
3. Unnikrishnan case : Right to education up to age fourteen under Article 21
4. Hussainara Khatoon case : Right to privacy
How many of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
questions.e: Hussainara Khatoon (1979) dealt with undertrial prisoners and led to recognition of the right to speedy trial and free legal aid under Article 21. The right to privacy was recognised in Puttaswamy (2017).
questions.u: Supreme Court, High Court & Subordinate Courts

questions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the independence of the judiciary:
1. The conduct of a Supreme Court judge can be freely discussed in Parliament.
2. The salaries and allowances of Supreme Court judges are charged on the Consolidated Fund of India.
3. A person who has held office as a judge of the Supreme Court is barred from pleading or acting in any court or before any authority in India.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Article 121 bars discussion of a judge's conduct in Parliament except on a motion for removal, so judges can decide without fear of political attack. Charged expenditure is not voted on, and Article 124(7) prevents retired judges from practising.
questions.u: Supreme Court, High Court & Subordinate Courts

questions.q:
Consider the following pairs:
High Court : Jurisdiction
1. Bombay High Court : Maharashtra, Goa and the Union Territory of Dadra and Nagar Haveli and Daman and Diu
2. Calcutta High Court : West Bengal and the Union Territory of Andaman and Nicobar Islands
3. Kerala High Court : Kerala and Puducherry
4. Madras High Court : Tamil Nadu and Puducherry
How many of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
questions.e: Kerala High Court has jurisdiction over Kerala and Lakshadweep, while Puducherry falls under the Madras High Court. Parliament can extend a High Court's jurisdiction to a Union Territory under Article 230.
questions.u: Supreme Court, High Court & Subordinate Courts

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Under Article 141, the law declared by the Supreme Court is binding on all courts within the territory of India.
2. Under Article 142, the Supreme Court may pass such decree or order as is necessary for doing complete justice in any cause or matter pending before it.
3. Special leave to appeal under Article 136 can be sought against the judgment of a court martial.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Articles 141 and 142 give the Supreme Court its binding precedent value and its power to do complete justice. Article 136(2) specifically excludes courts or tribunals constituted under laws relating to the Armed Forces from special leave jurisdiction.
questions.u: Supreme Court, High Court & Subordinate Courts

questions.q:
Statement-I: A judge of a High Court can be transferred from one High Court to another without his consent.
Statement-II: Article 222 empowers the President, after consultation with the Chief Justice of India, to transfer a judge from one High Court to any other High Court.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
o: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
questions.e: Article 222 does not require the judge's consent, only consultation with the CJI, and the Court has said that the transfer must be made in public interest and not as punishment. This also keeps judges from becoming too attached to local interests.
questions.u: Supreme Court, High Court & Subordinate Courts

questions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding Gram Nyayalayas:
1. They are established at the village panchayat level.
2. The Nyayadhikari presiding over a Gram Nyayalaya is appointed by the State Government in consultation with the High Court.
3. They have jurisdiction over both civil and criminal cases.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: The Gram Nyayalayas Act, 2008 provides for courts at the intermediate panchayat level or for a group of contiguous panchayats, to give access to justice at the doorstep. They try both civil and criminal matters.
questions.u: Supreme Court, High Court & Subordinate Courts

questions.q: Under the Judges (Inquiry) Act, 1968, a motion for removal of a Supreme Court judge must be given in writing to the Speaker of the Lok Sabha signed by at least _____ members of the Lok Sabha, or to the Chairman of the Rajya Sabha signed by at least _____ members of the Rajya Sabha.
questions.e: If the motion is admitted, a three-member committee of a Supreme Court judge, a High Court Chief Justice and a distinguished jurist investigates the charges. Justice V. Ramaswami's case in 1993 is the best-known example, where the motion failed in the Lok Sabha for lack of the required majority.
questions.s: Judges (Inquiry) Act, 1968; Laxmikanth, chapter on Supreme Court
questions.u: Supreme Court, High Court & Subordinate Courts

questions.q: Which one of the following is NOT a qualification for appointment as a Judge of the Supreme Court under Article 124(3)?
o: A judge of a High Court for at least five years
An advocate of a High Court for at least ten years
A distinguished jurist in the opinion of the President
A judicial officer in the subordinate judiciary for at least ten years
questions.e: Article 124(3) lists service as a High Court judge for five years, ten years as a High Court advocate, or being a distinguished jurist. Service in the subordinate judiciary alone does not qualify, unlike for the High Court under Article 217.
questions.u: Supreme Court, High Court & Subordinate Courts

questions.q:
Consider the following pairs:
Article : Provision
1. Article 126 : Appointment of acting Chief Justice of India
2. Article 127 : Attendance of retired judges at sittings of the Supreme Court
3. Article 128 : Appointment of ad hoc judges
4. Article 129 : Supreme Court to be a court of record
How many of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
questions.e: Article 127 provides for ad hoc judges and Article 128 for the attendance of retired judges, so the second and third pairs are swapped. Article 126 and Article 129 are correct.
questions.u: Supreme Court, High Court & Subordinate Courts
questions.h: 126 acting CJI, 127 ad hoc, 128 retired, 129 court of record

questions.q: Which Article of the Constitution gives every High Court the power of superintendence over all courts and tribunals within its territorial jurisdiction, other than those relating to the armed forces?
questions.e: Article 227 gives the supervisory power over courts and tribunals, while Article 226 deals with writs, Article 235 with control over the subordinate judiciary's personnel and Article 228 with transfer of cases involving constitutional questions to the High Court.
questions.u: Supreme Court, High Court & Subordinate Courts

questions.q: In the appointment of a Judge of a High Court, other than the Chief Justice, the President is required by Article 217 to consult
o: the Chief Justice of India and the Governor of the State only
the Chief Justice of India, the Governor of the State and the Chief Justice of the High Court
the Governor of the State and the Chief Justice of the High Court only
the Chief Justice of India and the Chief Justice of the High Court only
questions.e: For a Chief Justice of a High Court the consultation is with the CJI and the Governor, while for other judges the Chief Justice of that High Court is also consulted. In practice the collegium system decides the names.
questions.u: Supreme Court, High Court & Subordinate Courts

questions.q: A case involving a substantial question of law about the interpretation of the Constitution must be decided by a Supreme Court bench of at least how many judges, under Article 145(3)?
questions.e: Article 145(3) requires a minimum of five judges for such cases, and for any reference by the President under Article 143. This is the Constitution Bench.
questions.u: Supreme Court, High Court & Subordinate Courts

questions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the National Capital Territory of Delhi:
1. Article 239AA was inserted in the Constitution by the 69th Amendment Act.
2. The Legislative Assembly of Delhi can make laws on public order, police and land.
3. The Council of Ministers in Delhi cannot exceed ten percent of the total strength of the Legislative Assembly.
4. In 2018 a Constitution Bench of the Supreme Court held that the Lieutenant Governor has independent decision-making powers on all matters.
How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Article 239AA(3)(a) excludes entries 1, 2 and 18 of the State List (public order, police and land) from the Assembly's powers. The 2018 verdict held that the Lieutenant Governor is bound by the aid and advice of the Council of Ministers, except for matters he refers to the President, so he has no independent power over all subjects.

questions.q:
Which of the following Union Territories have a Legislative Assembly?
1. Delhi
2. Puducherry
3. Jammu and Kashmir
4. Ladakh
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
questions.e: Under the Jammu and Kashmir Reorganisation Act, 2019, Jammu and Kashmir became a Union Territory with a legislature and Ladakh became one without a legislature. Delhi's Assembly rests on Article 239AA and Puducherry's on Article 239A.

questions.q:
Consider the following pairs:
Constitutional Amendment : Related to
1. 10th Amendment : Incorporation of Dadra and Nagar Haveli as a Union Territory
2. 12th Amendment : Incorporation of Goa, Daman and Diu as a Union Territory
3. 13th Amendment : Creation of the Legislature for Puducherry
4. 69th Amendment : Special provisions for the National Capital Territory of Delhi
How many of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
questions.e: The Puducherry Legislature came with Article 239A through the 14th Amendment (1962). The 13th Amendment is linked to Nagaland (Article 371A).

questions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the Jammu and Kashmir Reorganisation Act, 2019:
1. It created two Union Territories, Jammu and Kashmir with a legislature and Ladakh without a legislature.
2. The new Union Territories came into existence on 31 October 2019.
3. In December 2023, a Constitution Bench of the Supreme Court upheld the President's order abrogating the special status under Article 370.
4. Ladakh has its own Legislative Assembly.
How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: The Act separated the former State into two Union Territories on 31 October 2019, the birth anniversary of Sardar Patel. The Supreme Court held Article 370 to be a temporary provision; Ladakh remains without a legislature.
questions.s: J&K Reorganisation Act, 2019; In re: Article 370, Supreme Court (11 Dec 2023)

questions.q: Under Article 240 of the Constitution, the President can make regulations for the peace, progress and good government of certain Union Territories. Which one of the following is NOT covered by this power?
o: Dadra and Nagar Haveli and Daman and Diu
questions.e: Article 240 covers Union Territories without legislatures, such as Andaman and Nicobar Islands, Lakshadweep and Dadra and Nagar Haveli and Daman and Diu, and also Puducherry when its Assembly is suspended or dissolved. Delhi has its own Assembly under Article 239AA.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the Lieutenant Governor of Delhi:
1. In case of a difference of opinion between the Lieutenant Governor and his Ministers on any matter, he shall refer it to the President for decision.
2. In the 2018 judgment, the Supreme Court held that the Lieutenant Governor is bound by the aid and advice of the Council of Ministers unless he refers a matter to the President.
3. The Delhi Legislative Assembly has the power to legislate on public order.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: The proviso to Article 239AA(4) provides this reference, and the Court said that difference must not be raised casually. Public order, police and land are outside the Assembly's competence.

questions.q:
Statement-I: Parliament can make laws on any subject in the State List for a Union Territory.
Statement-II: Article 246(4) empowers Parliament to make laws for any part of the territory of India not included in a State, notwithstanding that the matter is enumerated in the State List.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
o: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
questions.e: Since a Union Territory is not part of any State, the State List has no exclusive owner there. Parliament's power under Article 246(4) therefore reaches State List subjects, even in Union Territories having their own legislatures.

questions.q:
Consider the following pairs:
Feature : Borrowed from
1. Residuary powers with the Centre : Canada
2. Concurrent List : Australia
3. Suspension of Fundamental Rights during Emergency : Germany (Weimar Constitution)
4. Joint sitting of the two Houses of Parliament : United States
How many of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
questions.e: The Indian federation with a strong Centre and residuary powers with the Centre comes from Canada, and the Concurrent List and joint sitting both come from Australia, not the United States.
questions.s: Laxmikanth, chapter on Sources of the Constitution

questions.q:
Statement-I: A law made by Parliament cannot be declared invalid merely because it has extra-territorial operation.
Statement-II: Article 245(2) provides that no law made by Parliament shall be deemed invalid on the ground that it would have extra-territorial operation.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
o: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
questions.e: Article 245(2) allows Indian laws to apply to Indians and Indian interests abroad, whereas a State law operates only within the State unless a sufficient territorial nexus exists. This is the territorial nexus idea in the Constitution.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the doctrine of repugnancy under Article 254:
1. If a State law on a Concurrent List subject conflicts with a Union law, the Union law prevails.
2. A State law repugnant to a Union law on a Concurrent List subject prevails in that State if it has received the assent of the President.
3. Article 254 applies to conflicts on State List subjects.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Article 254(1) gives primacy to the Union law, with the exception in 254(2) for State laws reserved for and assented to by the President, though Parliament can later override it. State List subjects are not covered, since the State has exclusive power there, unless Parliament legislates under special provisions.

questions.q:
Match the following provisions with their descriptions:
A. Article 249
B. Article 250
C. Article 252
D. Article 253
1. Parliament may legislate on a State List subject if the Rajya Sabha passes a resolution in the national interest
2. Parliament may legislate on State List subjects while a Proclamation of Emergency is in operation
3. Parliament may legislate for two or more States by their consent
4. Parliament may legislate to implement international treaties and agreements
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
questions.e: These are the four special circumstances in which Parliament can step into the State List, apart from President's Rule. Article 249 needs a two-thirds Rajya Sabha resolution and lasts one year at a time.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the Inter-State Council:
1. It can be established by the President under Article 263 if it appears that the public interest would be served.
2. The Prime Minister is the Chairman of the Council.
3. It was first established in 1950.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Article 263 is enabling and not mandatory, so the Council is not permanent. It was set up in 1990 following the Sarkaria Commission's recommendation, and the Prime Minister chairs it.

questions.q: Which Article of the Constitution provides for the adjudication of disputes relating to the waters of inter-State rivers or river valleys?
questions.e: Article 262 allows Parliament to provide for adjudication of such disputes and to bar the courts from hearing them, which Parliament did through the Inter-State Water Disputes Act, 1956. Article 261 deals with full faith and credit, and Article 263 with the Inter-State Council.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding Zonal Councils:
1. They are constitutional bodies created under Article 263.
2. The Union Home Minister is the Chairman of each Zonal Council.
3. The North Eastern Council was established by a separate Act of Parliament in 1971.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Zonal Councils are statutory advisory bodies created under the States Reorganisation Act, 1956, not constitutional ones. Their purpose is regional cooperation; the north-eastern States have a separate Council set up in 1971.
questions.h: Zonal Councils: 1956 Act, not the Constitution

questions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the Goods and Services Tax Council:
1. The Union Finance Minister is the Chairperson of the Council.
2. The Centre has two-thirds of the weighted votes and the States together have one-third.
3. Every decision of the Council must be taken by a majority of not less than three-fourths of the weighted votes of the members present and voting.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Article 279A, inserted by the 101st Amendment, gives the Centre one-third of the weighted vote and the States together two-thirds. The three-fourths rule means that the Centre cannot pass a decision alone, and the States cannot do so without the Centre.

questions.q: Which Finance Commission recommended raising the share of the States in the net proceeds of Union taxes from 32 percent to 42 percent?
questions.e: The Fourteenth Finance Commission, which reported for 2015-20, increased the States' share to 42 percent to give States more untied funds and fiscal autonomy. The Thirteenth had recommended 32 percent.

questions.q:
Consider the following pairs:
Article : Provision
1. Article 267 : Contingency Fund of India
2. Article 270 : Taxes levied and collected by the Union and distributed between the Union and the States
3. Article 268 : Taxes levied and collected by the Union and distributed between the Union and the States
4. Article 280 : Goods and Services Tax Council
How many of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
questions.e: Article 268 deals with duties levied by the Union but collected and appropriated by the States, while the distribution described is in Article 270. The Goods and Services Tax Council is under Article 279A; Article 280 is the Finance Commission.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding a National Emergency under Article 352:
1. The President can proclaim it only on the written recommendation of the Union Cabinet.
2. A Proclamation must be approved by both Houses of Parliament within one month.
3. 'Internal disturbance' remains a ground for proclaiming it.
4. Once approved, it can be continued beyond six months by approval of Parliament at six-monthly intervals.
How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: The 44th Amendment (1978) required the Cabinet's written recommendation, cut the approval period from two months to one, and replaced 'internal disturbance' with 'armed rebellion'. All three changes responded to misuse of the power in 1975.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the effects of a National Emergency:
1. Article 19 is suspended automatically when an Emergency is proclaimed on the ground of war or external aggression.
2. The President can suspend the enforcement of the right to life and personal liberty under Article 21 by an order under Article 359.
3. The suspension of Article 19 under Article 358 operates throughout the country, while an order under Article 359 can be limited to a part of the country.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Since the 44th Amendment, Articles 20 and 21 cannot be suspended under Article 359, and Article 358 operates only for war or external aggression, not armed rebellion. Article 358 is automatic and countrywide, whereas Article 359 needs an order and can be local.

questions.q:
Statement-I: The 44th Amendment Act, 1978 replaced 'internal disturbance' with 'armed rebellion' as a ground for proclaiming a National Emergency.
Statement-II: The 44th Amendment sought to prevent the kind of misuse of Article 352 seen during the Emergency of 1975.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
o: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
questions.e: The 1975 Emergency was proclaimed on the vague ground of internal disturbance, which allowed a wide reading. Limiting the ground to armed rebellion makes it harder to use the provision for political ends.
questions.h: Cabinet writes, one month, armed rebellion

questions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding President's Rule under Article 356:
1. A Proclamation must be approved by both Houses of Parliament within one month.
2. It cannot be continued beyond a maximum of three years.
3. Its continuation beyond one year is possible only if a National Emergency is in operation and the Election Commission certifies that elections cannot be held.
4. Approval of the Proclamation requires a special majority in each House.
How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Approval is within two months by a simple majority of each House, and each approval lasts six months, up to three years. The extra conditions for going beyond one year were added by the 44th Amendment.

questions.q: Which one of the following was held by the Supreme Court in S. R. Bommai v. Union of India (1994)?
o: A Proclamation under Article 356 is subject to judicial review
The satisfaction of the President under Article 356 cannot be questioned in any court
Federalism is not a basic feature of the Constitution
The Centre can dismiss a State Government whenever it loses a majority in the Lok Sabha
questions.e: The nine-judge bench held that a Proclamation is justiciable, that the floor of the House is the place to test a majority, and that federalism and secularism are part of the basic structure. The Court can restore a dismissed Government if the Proclamation is found invalid.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding Financial Emergency under Article 360:
1. A Proclamation must be approved by both Houses of Parliament within two months.
2. It remains in force for a maximum of six months and cannot be extended further.
3. During its operation the President can direct reduction of the salaries and allowances of all or any class of persons serving the Union or a State, including High Court and Supreme Court judges.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Unlike National Emergency, a Financial Emergency has no outer time limit, and continues until revoked once approved. The power to cut salaries and to direct States to observe financial propriety is the main consequence.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding trade, commerce and intercourse:
1. Article 301 declares that trade, commerce and intercourse throughout the territory of India shall be free.
2. Parliament may impose restrictions on the freedom of trade between States in the public interest.
3. A State Legislature can impose reasonable restrictions on the freedom of trade within the State in public interest without the previous sanction of the President.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Under Article 304(b), a Bill imposing such restrictions can be introduced in a State Legislature only with the previous sanction of the President. This keeps States from building trade barriers that would break the economic unity of the country.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding Commissions on Centre-State relations:
1. The Sarkaria Commission was appointed in 1983.
2. The Sarkaria Commission submitted its report in 1988.
3. The Sarkaria Commission recommended the abolition of Article 356.
4. The Punchhi Commission on Centre-State relations was constituted in 2007.
How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Sarkaria (1983 to 1988) said Article 356 should be used very sparingly, as a last resort, and not abolished. The Punchhi Commission, chaired by a former Chief Justice of India, was set up in 2007 to look at the subject again.

questions.q: Which Article of the Constitution states that where a State fails to comply with the directions given by the Union in the exercise of its executive power, the President may hold that a situation has arisen in which the government of the State cannot be carried on in accordance with the Constitution?
questions.e: Article 365 links disobedience of Union directions to a failure of constitutional machinery, which then opens the way to President's Rule under Article 356. Article 355 is the general duty of the Union to protect States.

questions.q:
Consider the following pairs:
Article : State/Region
1. Article 371A : Nagaland
2. Article 371F : Mizoram
3. Article 371H : Goa
4. Article 371J : Karnataka (Hyderabad-Karnataka region)
How many of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
questions.e: Article 371F is for Sikkim, 371G for Mizoram, 371H for Arunachal Pradesh and 371I for Goa. Articles 371A and 371J are correctly matched.
questions.h: 371A Nagaland, F Sikkim, G Mizoram, H Arunachal, I Goa, J Karnataka

questions.q: Which one of the following subjects was transferred from the State List to the Concurrent List by the 42nd Amendment Act, 1976?
questions.e: The 42nd Amendment moved five subjects to the Concurrent List: education, forests, protection of wild animals and birds, weights and measures, and administration of justice. Police, agriculture and public health remain in the State List.

questions.q:
Which of the following subjects are in the Concurrent List?
1. Forests
2. Insurance
3. Trade unions
4. Banking
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
questions.e: Forests and trade unions are Concurrent List subjects, while insurance and banking are in the Union List, which is why Parliament alone legislates on them.
